exceptions.reason: The retiring gateway must keep its upstream provider clients until its callers and deployment are decommissioned; it is not a reusable Fleet client.
The product trains and runs its own local model, and its optional evaluation harness uses native Python or Swift clients where a JavaScript package cannot apply.
The ingestion runtime is Python and now requires an explicit project-owned free-provider or local endpoint, key, and model; the JavaScript Vercel AI SDK is not applicable to this runtime.

The desktop product performs provider calls inside its Rust trust boundary and now exposes only explicit local or provider-owned routes; a JavaScript model client would cross the product security boundary.
The media pipeline is Python and now uses an explicit direct free-provider endpoint without gateway metadata; the JavaScript Vercel AI SDK is not applicable to this runtime.
The Apple-native product uses URLSession for local and user-selected direct endpoints inside its Swift runtime; the JavaScript Vercel AI SDK is not applicable.
The operator-side Python pipeline talks only to local MLX and LM Studio inference servers; the JavaScript Vercel AI SDK is not applicable.
This Worker calls the dedicated moderation endpoint, which is not a Vercel AI SDK text-generation surface; it remains isolated from the Fleet model-routing contract.

ratifiedDecision: Fleet does not use a shared AI gateway. JavaScript and TypeScript model callers use the pinned Vercel AI SDK against a project-owned free-provider or local endpoint wherever the runtime supports it. Native runtimes keep explicit project-owned clients. Direct provider calls are routing evidence, while the retired gateway host and gateway-only environment variables are blocking findings.
